title: capacity-reserve-orchestration-and-fallback-ownership-sprint
summary: Sprint planning to finalize a regional reserve/capacity orchestration prototype, assign fallback and runbook ownership, and agree on a dry-run date for launch gating. Tradeoffs discussed: cost of reserved pools vs. latency SLOs, KV cache impact and fallback model skew. Action items and owners assigned.
topics: fallback model variants and automatic degrade paths
action_items: Aisha: build prototype of region-aware reserve allocator (alpha) and share architecture doc - due 2027-05-25
Jonas: update SLO appendix with staged eviction thresholds and cost/latency projection - due 2027-05-18
Sofia: create a release checklist for dry-run that includes KV cache warmup steps and telemetry hooks - due 2027-05-20
Liam: schedule cross-team dry-run and invite Sales/Support for comms rehearsal - due 2027-05-21
Maya: consolidate fallback policy matrix and distribute for review - due 2027-05-17
next_steps: Share prototype doc link in #launch-readiness channel
Run short benchmark of reserve allocator vs current autoscale (tokens/sec, p95) and post results
Follow-up sync to review telemetry from canary once prototype is in staging
transcript:
Header: 2027-05-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Jonas Patel, Aisha Rahman, Liam O'Neill, Sofia Martinez, Ethan Grant, Priya Desai, Noah Kim

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Align on a reserve capacity prototype, hand off runbooks, schedule dry-run.

[00:00] Maya: ok, let's kick off. thanks everyone for carving time. main goals today are to decide ownership for the reserve allocator prototype and to lock a dry-run date for the launch gating.
[00:18] Ethan: quick note — execs want a clear rollback story and an SLA-ish number we can point to. not necessarily a contract yet, but something operational.
[00:30] Jonas: got it. from SRE side what we need is a policy that says when staged eviction kicks in, and clear telemetry hooks. otherwise alerts will blow up.
[00:45] Aisha: i sketched an allocator that maintains a regional reserve pool and exposes an admission control API. it will prefer warm kv cache instances for high-qps routes to avoid cold-start latency. (laughs) i wrote KV cash in the doc, sorry.
[01:05] Liam: the big tradeoff is cost — reserved pools increase commit cost. we need to show benefit vs current burst autoscale. can we run a quick sim?
[01:20] Aisha: yes, i can run a sim. i want to measure p50/p95 token latency and tokens/sec under a 30% sustained bump. i'll also include cold vs warm kv cache numbers.
[01:38] Priya: region-aware routing matters — if we reserve in us-west and traffic goes to eu, that's wasted. we need regional caps and a fallback to cross-region routing with graceful degrade.
[01:55] Noah: plus the oncall playbook needs explicit steps: if cross-region fallback trips, who pages, what's the fallback model order.
[02:10] Sofia: i'll add a flow to the release checklist: warmup sequences, KV cache prefetch, and synthetic traffic validators. also telemetry flags to mark reserve hits.
[02:30] Maya: rough ask: prototype alpha in two weeks, dry-run in two weeks after that. is that realistic?
[02:42] Jonas: two weeks for alpha is tight but doable if we scope to admission control + metrics. no full autoscaler integration yet.
[02:55] Aisha: agreed. i'll scope it to allocator + admission endpoint + a small simulator. no live rollout.
[03:10] Ethan: remember to include fallback policy in the doc — e.g., fallback to quantized model variant before cross-region routing to save cost.
[03:25] Liam: that's a good point — fallback order matrix: 1) smaller quantized model in-region, 2) cross-region higher capacity, 3) degrade response quality. we should rank by latency impact and cost.
[03:45] Maya: can someone volunteer to own the fallback matrix?
[03:50] Aisha: i'll take the technical draft.
[03:53] Maya: excellent. who owns the runbook?
[03:56] Jonas: i'll own the runbook for oncall operations. Sofia will handle release steps.
[04:05] Sofia: yep. i'll also make a small checklist that the product can sign-off on before dry-run.
[04:15] [minor crosstalk] Speaker 1: ...yeah that makes sense...
[04:35] Maya: ok, let's talk telemetry. we need token-level counters, reserve-hit counters, and per-model p95. also traceable request ids that propagate.
[04:50] Jonas: we'll add reserve_hit and reserve_miss metrics. question: do we instrument admission rejects with reason codes? that helps SLO analysis.
[05:05] Aisha: yes, reason codes: capacity, kv_warmth, routing_penalty. but note kv_warmth is estimated by a heuristic, not perfect. you will see noise.
[05:22] Ethan: put that caveat in the doc so stakeholders don't misread noise as failure.
[05:30] Liam: one of the stakeholders asked if we could short-circuit to a cached response for certain non-critical prompts. is that something we can add later?
[05:45] Aisha: that's more of an application-level cache. we can include it as a follow-up, not in alpha.
[06:00] Priya: on the orchestration side, we need a simple policy language: min_reserve, burst_window, regional_preference. we should avoid complex DSLs at first.
[06:15] Jonas: agreed. simpler is better for ops. also include a safety cap to prevent infinite reserve consumption.
[06:30] Maya: how does this interact with Dedicated vs Hosted? we have customers that will want dedicated pools.
[06:45] Aisha: model is the same but placement differs. Dedicated will map reserves to a tenant pool; hosted will be multitenant with per-route reservations. alpha will only target hosted routes.
[07:00] Ethan: we should flag enterprise requirements — encryption at rest, KMS integration, audit logs for reserve usage. that's a compliance ask.
[07:15] Sofia: i'll add KMS and audit-log items to the checklist; we won't implement full HSM for alpha but note requirements.
[07:28] [30s pause/typing] Speaker 2: (unintelligible)
[07:50] Maya: okay next — fallback model variants. we need to decide which models are acceptable fallbacks per route. this ties to model catalog.
[08:05] Aisha: i'll produce a fallback mapping: route -> primary model, fallback1 -> quantized variant, fallback2 -> smaller architecture. note that quant skews can cause hallucinations in some generation tasks. we'll include guardrails.
[08:25] Liam: add an eval set to measure divergence after fallback. if divergence > threshold, we prefer cross-region rather than degrade quality.
[08:40] Noah: second the eval set. the oncall runbook should include a rollback threshold based on eval regressions.
[08:55] Maya: yes — rollback triggers: delta p95 > X, eval divergence > Y, or error rate spike. we need explicit numbers before dry-run.
[09:10] Jonas: propose p95 increase > 30% as a hard trigger, and eval divergence > 5% as soft trigger for manual review.
[09:25] Ethan: that seems reasonable. we should validate with historical traffic.
[09:38] [background keyboard] Speaker 3: i think the cost model is the sticky part...
[09:50] Liam: cost model — we need a spreadsheet that shows per-token cost for reserve vs autoscale at different burst shapes. i'll own that.
[10:05] Maya: great. add a column that shows break-even burst length.
[10:15] Aisha: on the allocator internals, i want to keep the admission logic simple: check reserve, check kv_warmth score, check route SLO, then allow or forward. it will return a decision and reason codes.
[10:35] Jonas: can the admission API provide a suggested wait time for queued requests? helpful for client SDKs.
[10:45] Aisha: we can add a hint but it's best-effort. SDKs should treat it as advisory.
[10:55] Priya: for regional capacities, set soft limits that allow bursting into neighboring regions up to X% to preserve latency SLOs. we need to param that per-region.
[11:12] Maya: okay, let's timebox discussion on the runbook handoff — runbook should have: who to page, fallback order, metrics dashboard link, rollback steps, communication templates.
[11:28] Jonas: i suggest a shortplay that lists immediate steps on page: 1) check reserve_hit and reserve_miss, 2) check admission reject codes, 3) switch fallback priority to cross-region if safe.
[11:45] Sofia: i'll draft the communication templates: slack page message, incident summary template, customer comms blurbs.
[12:00] [short laughter] Speaker 1: we will not write the customer letter until we have numbers...
[12:15] Maya: what's the consensus on the dry-run date? suggested 2027-05-28 as a 2-hour window.
[12:25] Liam: i can do that date. schedule for 14:00-16:00 UTC?
[12:32] Ethan: works for execs.
[12:36] Noah: oncall okay with that window.
[12:40] Maya: perfect. action items then.
[12:45] [Auto-generated action items inserted]
[13:00] Aisha: i wanted to mention quant skew — in our tests some prompts degrade more than others. we'll attach a short list of sensitive prompts to the eval doc.
[13:15] Liam: add a column on the spreadsheet that notes prompt sensitivity so stakeholders can prioritize.
[13:28] Priya: is there any dependency on the scheduler rollout next sprint? because that might change how reserve interacts with pods.
[13:42] Jonas: minor dependency. i'll coordinate with scheduler team. shouldn't block alpha.
[13:55] Maya: good. who will present the dry-run outcomes? product or infra?
[14:05] Ethan: infra should present the operations view; product should present customer impact. joint presentation.
[14:18] Sofia: i'll set a slide template for ops + product and share.
[14:30] [brief pause] Speaker 2: (mutter)
[14:45] Maya: ok any high-risk open concerns?
[14:50] Noah: the real risk is eviction policy causing cascading falls in other tenants if we mis-tune the safety cap. we need a rapid isolation path.
[15:05] Jonas: we can implement a tenant isolation switch to quickly disable reserve consumption for a tenant if we detect cross-tenant spill.
[15:18] Aisha: and we should limit reserve per-tenant to a small percentage initially. that reduces blast radius.
[15:33] Liam: i'll add that to the cost and risk spreadsheet.
[15:45] Maya: final recap before we wrap — owners and dates. Aisha prototype by 5/25, Jonas SLO appendix by 5/18, Sofia release checklist by 5/20, Liam schedule dry-run by 5/21 and cost spreadsheet by 5/24, Maya consolidate fallback matrix by 5/17.
[16:05] Ethan: i'll want a short exec one-pager before the dry-run. can someone produce that?
[16:12] Maya: I'll draft the one-pager and circulate.
[16:20] Priya: i'll review compliance items — KMS, audit logs — and mark must-haves for Dedicated customers.
[16:30] [closing] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll track action items in the sprint board and meet briefly next Tuesday to check progress.
[16:40] [meeting ends]

Questions (auto):
- What are the rollback triggers? (answered: p95 >30%, eval divergence>5%)
- Who owns runbook? (Jonas, Sofia for release)
